title: Customer Usage Alert & Response Grid
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is a pragmatic grid for QBRs: quickly classify recent client usage spikes, map them to root causes, estimate short-term cost exposure, and recommend specific mitigation or escalation steps. Designed for one-page summary slides plus an appendix for detailed token tables.

Audience:
- CS leads preparing QBRs
- Renewal owners evaluating spend risk
- Solutions & SRE on-call for rate-limit incidents

How to use: (quick steps)
1) Pull client token/time series for the last 90 days (hourly if possible).
2) Compute 7/30/90 day medians and 95th percentile peaks.
3) Use the grid below to classify the spike and pick the recommended response.
4) Draft an action row for the QBR: owner, ETA, and success criteria.

Executive summary template (first slide bullets):
- Top-line: 90-day token growth +% vs prior period and estimated next 30-day spend at current run-rate.
- Risk: probability bucket (low/medium/high) of hitting reserve/spend guard in next 14 days.
- Ask: immediate throttle? rate-limit adjustment? renewal cadence change?

SENSITIVITY & RESPONSE GRID (use this to pick actions)
Columns: Incident type | Typical signal | Cost exposure (est USD next 7d) | Immediate CS action | Engineering action | Escalation path | QBR talking point

Rows (examples):
1) Legit growth (onboarding surge) | Sustained ramp across endpoints, users increasing, embeddings up | Low–Medium (predictable) | Confirm growth origin, offer optimization suggestions (batching, caching) | Recommend quantization or dedicated routing if sustained | No immediate escalation; note for Dedicated discussion | "Customer adoption spike driven by CRM pilot; recommend dedicated capacity conversation."

2) Reward-loop bug / runaway prompt | Sudden jump in tokens per request, identical endpoint | High (fast burn) | Pause offending route, notify customer success and engineering, provide remediation template | Hotfix to prompt wrapper, autosanitizer rule | Pager to infra/serving-runtime on-call | "Transient runaway prompt; mitigated via prompt length caps and rate cap until code fix."

3) Integration test or bot misconfig | Very high qps but low unique users, lots of repeated identical requests | Medium–High | Apply temporary app-level rate cap, ask for sandboxing, propose client-side debounce | Suggest adding client-token or IP-based throttle heuristics | Escalate to solutions engineering for API contract changes | "Automated integration causing bursts; suggest token quota and client SDK debounce."

4) Third-party spam/abuse | Traffic from unusual geos/IP clusters; high error/latency | Medium | Open abuse case with customer, add IP blocklist guidance | Add geo-fence or stricter auth checks | Security team notification; possible ACLs | "Abuse detected; implemented mitigations and monitoring."

5) Billing anomaly/unexpected pricing change | Consumption appears normal but bill projection spikes | High | Immediate audit of invoice items, validate model variants used (e.g., 1.0 -> 2.0), ask finance for provisional credit if internal error | Build billing replay for last 30 days to find misattributed SKUs | Escalate to billing ops + finance | "Detected variant mismatch leading to cost delta; working to reconcile and credit."

DATA TABLES (appendix suggestions)
- Hourly token series CSV (attach as a separate sheet)
- Top 10 routes by token contribution (last 30 days)
- Token-per-request histogram (to spot runaway prompts)
- 95th percentile latency vs tokens (to identify long tail costs)

ALERT THRESHOLD SUGGESTIONS (examples to include in client config)
- Soft alert: 3x 7-day median projected 7-day spend > $1,000 -> CS notification email
- Hard alert: projection exceeds $10,000 in next 7 days or burn rate > 10k tokens/sec sustained for 1 hour -> Pager to on-call + customer notification
- Budget guard: auto-block if forecasted 72-hour spend > committed reserve plus buffer -> trigger billing block workflow (requires legal/finance)

QBR SLIDE FRAMEWORK (1 slide)
- Left: 90-day chart (tokens/day) + annotation for spike events
- Middle: Top 3 routes contributing to spend and short notes (onboarding, bug, test)
- Right: Recommended actions (Immediate, 30-day, Renewal ask)

SAMPLE CUSTOMER-SAFE MESSAGE (send after you take action)
"Hi <Customer>, we noticed a sudden increase in calls to <route>. We paused the route briefly and implemented a temporary rate cap to prevent unexpected charges. Our analysis suggests this was caused by <likely cause>. Next steps: we can help put a longer-term guard (quota or dedicated capacity) if you'd like. -- <CS rep>"

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOS (notes for CS owner)
- Can we add an automated 95th percentile forecast to the billing dashboard? (ticketed: JIRA-CS-4281)
- Should we offer a standard "onboarding burst" grant (1 week free buffer) as a renewal incentive?
- Confirm whether finance will support provisional credits for clear platform-side billing mismatch.

ACTION ITEM TEMPLATE (one row per QBR)
- Owner: <name>
- Issue: <short description>
- Immediate action taken: <what CS/engineering did>
- 30-day fix: <plan>
- Success criteria: <metric to close>
- Follow-up date: <YYYY-MM-DD>

Appendix: quick commands & queries
- Sample BigQuery: SELECT hour, SUM(tokens) FROM logs WHERE project_id = '<client>' GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;
- Kibana filter: route:<route> AND client_id:<client> | visualize tokens per minute

Notes to self / draft language (messy OK):
- Keep this doc as a minimal grid — we want to avoid overwhelming customers with raw numbers in QBRs.
- Engineering owners: if we ask for a hotfix, include expected time-to-rollback.
- Use "budget guard" language in renewal slides when customer shows repeated spikes; ties to Dedicated conversation.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12 A. Patel - created initial grid and examples.
- 2025-12-02 M. Lopez - added billing anomaly row and alert thresholds examples.
